Taylor Wimpey Cuts Sales Guidance as Housing Market Headwinds Persist
By Anthony O. Goriainoff

Taylor Wimpey cut its sales guidance after a decline in its net private sales rate, warning that housing market challenges persisted during the fall selling season as rising mortgage rates and living costs pressured affordability.

In the June 29 to Nov. 8 period, the home builder's net private sales rate per outlet per week--a key industry metric--fell to 0.60 from 0.63 last year, with a cancellation rate of 17% flat on the year prior. Excluding the impact of bulk deals, the net private sales rate was 0.54, down from 0.61.
For the year to date, the rate declined to 0.69 from 0.72 in the same period last year. Excluding bulk deals, the rate fell to 0.62 from 0.68.
Its order book, excluding joint ventures, as of Sunday stood at around 1.98 billion pounds ($2.64 billion), down from 2.12 billion pounds, representing 6,839 homes, a fall from 7,253 the year before.
Taylor Wimpey said that it now expects sales for the year, excluding joint ventures, to be around 10,500 homes, down from a previous guidance range of 10,600 to 10,800 homes.
The board now expects group adjusted operating profit--a key metric for the company--to be around the bottom end of the company-compiled consensus range of 262 million to 299 million pounds.
"Whilst affordability challenges continue to impact near-term demand, we continue to deliver progress on the operational priorities within our control," it said.
